title: Rivers of mud and boulders hit a Swiss village in 2017, yet no one there was hurt
body: On 23 August 2017 about 3.1 million m³ of rock crashed down from Pizzo Cengalo into Val Bondasca, in the Swiss canton of Grisons, burying eight hikers on the trail below. Rock and mud then kept pouring down the valley as **debris flows**, fast-moving slurries of water, mud and boulders. Around 500,000 m³ of debris reached the village of Bondo, filling the retention basin built to catch such debris and damaging many buildings and much of the village’s infrastructure. Yet there were no deaths or injuries where people lived.

cover.alt: A village road beside a wall, with a wooden barn and a white house just beyond a bank of grey rubble under a blue sky

slides.alt: Filmed from a village road, a surge of grey rubble and boulders rolls in behind a wall: a wooden barn tips over and is swept away in a cloud of dust, and the flow keeps churning past the houses as dust drifts across the valley.
slides.caption: A debris flow surges into Bondo on 23 August 2017: a wooden barn is knocked over and carried off as rubble and dust pour past the houses.

slides.question: How did the debris that reached Bondo compare with the rock that fell from the peak?
slides.explanation: About 500,000 m³ of debris flowed down to Bondo, roughly a sixth of the 3.1 million m³ of rock that crashed from the peak.
